prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. ONE original battle-ready enemy sprite illustration for an industrial fantasy action RPG: M21 Missing-Phase Jumper from a powerless underground hangar. A compact FOUR-LEGGED jumping machine-mineral creature: exactly four widely spread jointed feet with large visible compressed coil springs, arranged like an opening and closing four-point STAR around a small angular capacitor core. One flexible severed electrical cable forms a single dragging tail with a capped metal connector; the tail is visibly different from the four load-bearing spring legs. No spider abdomen, no extra legs, no humanoid elements. Coiled springs crouch ready to leap, copper contacts around the small central chassis hint at a brief electric ring upon landing. A few restrained pale cyan electrical highlights on ceramic capacitor blocks, no electric halo and no particle burst obscuring the body. Coal-black steel, faded ochre casing, oxidized copper joints, ivory ceramic insulators, slight mineral-organic fibers tucked into seams. Premium richly hand-painted stylized industrial-fantasy, beautiful functional engineering, broad clear light/shadow masses and tactile limited surface wear. Elevated three-quarter camera looking down 40 degrees, all four spring feet clearly distinguishable. Entire subject and cable tail framed with generous transparent margin; recognizably four-point star at 70 pixels. Nearly opaque solid subject on genuine transparent alpha; no ground, floor, cast shadow, pedestal, environment, lettering, labels, logo, UI, watermark, decorative border or any existing game creature.

alpha_validation.notes: Original generated alpha preserved; broad subject is nearly opaque. Transparent pixels may retain RGB visible in alpha-ignoring viewers.

visual_inspection: Exactly four spring legs and one distinct trailing cable are visible.
Four-point opening silhouette and compressed springs communicate the jump.
Ceramic capacitor core and restrained cyan accents support electric landing identity.
production_status: Single battle-ready illustration. Full directional animation, attacks, recovery and 70-pixel in-engine visual QA remain separate deliverables.
